open_points.subject: Trial corpus growth and current Activation
open_points.text: “activation, which requires an `admitted` verdict over the current corpus”; “Each contract version has a trial corpus”; “the corpus only grows”; admission and activation occur “when an implementation is submitted”
open_points.question: When adding or capturing a trial case changes the current corpus, what happens to an existing activation whose admission covered the previous corpus?
options: The activation remains runnable until another implementation is submitted
New runs are refused until the active implementation is resubmitted, admitted over the new corpus and activated again
The kernel automatically tests the active implementation on the enlarged corpus and either preserves or replaces its activation
open_points.default_guess: Keep the activation record but refuse new runs using it until the implementation is admitted over the current corpus.

open_points.subject: AdmissionVerdict
open_points.text: “a verdict for the same implementation and corpus is the same verdict” contradicts “every active case of the corpus is run again for the implementation at admission time, and the verdict covers exactly those executions” and TrialExecutions are separately minted observations
open_points.question: When the same implementation is submitted again against the unchanged corpus, is its admission the existing value or a new verdict associated with newly minted TrialExecutions?
options: Return the existing verdict and do not rerun its cases
Rerun the cases and create a distinct AdmissionVerdict entity
Rerun the cases but replace or mutate the existing verdict's TrialExecution references
open_points.default_guess: Rerun the cases and create a distinct admission record, since its evidence consists of new observations.

open_points.subject: ProofResult
open_points.text: “proving the same version gives the same result” contradicts “whether a flow version whose proof failed because a binding was not yet accepted can be proven again later — closed by A05 (yes)”
open_points.question: What identifies a ProofResult when the same immutable flow version can have different results after a referenced binding changes from proposed to accepted?
options: ProofResult identity includes the binding states or other proof context
Each proof invocation produces a distinct result entity
ProofResult is only an ephemeral computed answer whose equality is all returned facts, not the flow version
open_points.default_guess: Treat it as an ephemeral value identified by all returned facts and recompute it from current binding state.

open_points.subject: NodeExecution
open_points.text: M23 declares “Identity: value” and “an attempt's record is issued once,” while M07 says an execution observation that is “issued once” is an entity because “a value has no identifier of its own”; M23 is addressed by `run_id`, `node_id`, `map_index` and `attempt_number`
open_points.question: Is a NodeExecution an entity identified by its attempt coordinates, or a substitutable value identified by all of its facts?
options: An entity with the composite identity `(run_id, node_id, map_index, attempt_number)`
A value identified by all meaning facts
An entity with a separately minted identifier
open_points.default_guess: Treat it as an entity with the composite attempt identity.

open_points.subject: FlowNode.node_id
open_points.question: Who chooses or mints a node's `node_id`, and is it submitted as authored flow content or assigned by the kernel?
options: The composing agent supplies it as part of the immutable graph
The kernel assigns it while accepting the composition
It is derived from the node's meaning facts
open_points.default_guess: The composing agent supplies the node ID as part of the flow-version content.
